jsonld.description: Free iPhone app: measure card centering line by line, zoom into corners and edges, and check if a card is worth the grading fee. PSA, BGS and CGC references.
featureList: Card centering measurement from a photo
Guided line-by-line border check with a loupe
PSA, BGS and CGC centering reference comparison
Worth Grading? profit and break-even calculator
Corner and edge close-ups from the original photo
Batch scanning and submission checklist PDF

mainEntity.name: Can CenterMint measure a card in a sleeve, top loader or graded slab?

acceptedAnswer.text: Automatic measurement works on raw cards only. A sleeve, top loader or slab adds its own edges and glare, so the app would be measuring plastic instead of the card. When it detects a sleeve, it tells you and switches to manual alignment, where you line up the four card edges yourself. For the most accurate result, take the card out and rescan.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is the centering measurement?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the photo and on the lines you confirm. Small shifts matter: with 3 mm borders on each side, going from 50/50 to 55/45 moves the artwork only 0.3 mm. CenterMint fits gold and silver borders edge by edge at sub-pixel level and flags the lines it is unsure about, but it does not claim a single accuracy percentage. Check flagged lines in the loupe and retake blurry or glary photos.

mainEntity.name: What centering does a PSA 10 need?

acceptedAnswer.text: PSA’s published Gem Mint 10 guideline is approximately 55/45 or better on the front and 75/25 or better on the back. PSA 9 is approximately 60/40 on the front and 90/10 on the back. BGS and CGC publish their own scales, and some figures apply only to certain card categories. Centering is one of several criteria, so good centering alone does not guarantee a grade. Check the official pages before submitting.

mainEntity.name: How does Worth Grading? decide whether a card is worth grading?

acceptedAnswer.text: For each grade it calculates: extra money = (graded price − raw price) × (1 − selling fee) − grading fee. The selling fee is paid whether you sell raw or graded, so only the price difference is reduced by it. The break-even top-grade price is raw price + grading fee ÷ (1 − selling fee). If even the second grade (such as PSA 9) makes money, the answer is worth grading; if only the top grade pays, it depends on corners and surface; if no grade pays, or centering rules out the grade that pays, it is not worth grading. The app never estimates the chance of a 10.

mainEntity.name: Does CenterMint look up eBay or other market prices?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The app does not connect to eBay or any price service and does not guess prices. You enter recent sold prices yourself, and they are saved on your device for that card. In Japan, buttons open Mercari sold listings and Yahoo! Auctions closed listings for the card name and number.

mainEntity.name: Does CenterMint check corners, edges and surface?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Corner & Edge Close-ups crop the four corners and four edges from your original photo at full resolution so you can inspect them yourself. The app does not score them, and a phone photo can miss tiny flaws, so check doubtful spots under a loupe and bright light.

mainEntity.name: What is free and what needs Pro?

acceptedAnswer.text: Free: centering measurement at full resolution, the loupe, the guided line check, PSA/BGS/CGC reference comparison, one batch of up to 5 cards, and the pre-grading check (Worth Grading? and close-ups) on one card of your choice. Pro adds those pre-grading tools for every card, the Submission Log, batch scanning, the decision assistant with a submission checklist PDF, CSV and 4K exports, presets and no ads.

mainEntity.name: Is CenterMint affiliated with PSA, BGS or CGC?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. CenterMint is an independent app. Its centering references follow the companies’ published standards for comparison only, and an actual grade can differ.

Measurement runs on your iPhone without an account. Photos are uploaded only if you opt in to correction sharing (off by default) or accept the one-time batch learning notice, which you can decline. Prices and the Submission Log stay on the device.

jsonld.name: How to measure card centering with CenterMint

step.text: Take the card out of its sleeve and lay it flat on a plain mat that contrasts with the border. Photograph it in even light, or import a photo or scan.
CenterMint suggests the outer card edge and the printed inner border. If any line is uncertain, it walks you through those lines one by one with the loupe and tells you why.
Confirm or nudge each line. The left/right and top/bottom ratios update as you go.
Measure the back as well and compare both sides with the PSA, BGS or CGC reference.
Before you submit, look through the corner and edge close-ups and run Worth Grading? with recent sold prices.

hero.lede: Measure the borders, check every line the app is unsure about, then decide whether the card is worth the grading fee.
hero.intro: CenterMint is an iPhone app for trading-card and sports-card collectors. It measures left/right and top/bottom centering from a photo of a raw card, compares the result with the published PSA, BGS and CGC centering references, and helps you decide before you pay to grade. It is an independent tool: it measures centering only and does not predict a full grade.

new.intro: Version 1.9 adds tools for the decision that costs money: is this card worth sending in?

features.title: Guided line check
features.body: When a line needs a second look, the editor takes you through the least certain lines one at a time. The loupe jumps to each line; tap “Looks Right” to move on, or drag the line where it belongs.

features.title: Why a line needs checking
features.body: Each step says why in plain words: glare, blur, a dark or low-resolution photo, a mat close to the card’s edge color, or no printed border found. If a retake would fix it, the app says so.

features.title: Worth Grading?
features.body: Enter the raw, PSA 9 and PSA 10 sold prices (or the BGS and CGC equivalents), your grading fee and the selling fee. CenterMint shows how much more or less you would make than selling raw, and the lowest top-grade price that breaks even. Grades your centering cannot reach are left out. You type the prices; in Japan, one tap opens Mercari and Yahoo! Auctions sold listings.

features.title: Corner & Edge Close-ups
features.body: Crops all four corners and the middle of all four edges from the original photo at full resolution, so you can zoom in for whitening and dings and share a collage. The app shows the close-ups; it does not score corners or surface.

features.title: Submission Log
features.body: Record each submission, what it cost and the grades that came back. See your top-grade rate, total grading fees, and whether returned grades stayed within the centering ceiling the app measured.

measure.h2: Measuring that tells you when to look closer
items: Automatic measurement for raw cards, with edge-by-edge sub-pixel fitting on gold and silver borders and a more reliable outer edge on cloth and patterned mats.
Cards in sleeves, top loaders or graded slabs are measured by lining up the four edges yourself. When the app detects a sleeve, it tells you and switches to manual alignment.
Loupe 2.0 shows real pixels with a pixel grid and an edge profile, and links opposite edges so you can compare both sides.
Every measurement uses the full-resolution photo, in the free version too.
Share images put your card photo first, with a small logo in the corner.

Batch 2.0 (Pro): shoot a stack in a row, show only the cards that need checking, sort by centering and save in one go. The decision assistant sorts cards into Submit, Fix first (such as an unmeasured back) and Below target, and exports a submission checklist PDF.

free: Front and back centering measurement at full resolution
Loupe and the guided line check, with the reason each line needs a look
Comparison with PSA, BGS and CGC centering references
Local library with front/back pairing, and share images
One batch of up to 5 cards
Worth Grading? and Corner & Edge Close-ups on one card of your choice
pro: Worth Grading? and Corner & Edge Close-ups for every card
Decision assistant with a submission checklist PDF
Centering report, 4K image enhancement and 4K exports
pricing.note: Pro is offered as monthly or yearly subscriptions or a one-time purchase; plans and local prices are shown in the app. Subscriptions renew automatically until canceled in your Apple Account settings.

items: It does not grade corners, edges, surface or authenticity, and it does not predict a PSA, BGS or CGC grade or the chance of a 10.
It does not guarantee a grading result. Centering references follow the published standards for comparison only. CenterMint is not affiliated with PSA, Beckett, CGC, Pokémon or any card publisher.
It does not fetch or estimate prices and does not connect to eBay. Worth Grading? uses the prices you enter.
Automatic measurement is for raw cards. On full-art cards without a printed border, the inner lines follow the art frame and the result is a reference only.
limits.privacy: Measurement runs on your iPhone and needs no account. Card photos leave the device only if you opt in: correction sharing is off by default, and batch import asks once before uploading, which you can decline. Prices you enter and your Submission Log stay on the device. See the privacy policy for details.
limits.languages: The app is available in English, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese.
